evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants in randomized curcumin anxiety trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2024 meta-analysis of eight randomized trials involving 567 participants found a pooled improvement in anxiety symptom scores with curcumin versus control.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; positive direction with very high heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Between-study heterogeneity was very high, so the pooled direction should not be presented as a uniform or high-certainty anxiolytic effect across formulations or populations.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants in randomized curcumin cognition trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 meta-analysis of nine randomized trials involving 501 participants reported an overall global-cognition signal with curcumin, with stronger pooled effects in studies lasting at least 24 weeks and in participants aged 60 years or older.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; duration- and age-modified cognition signal
evidence.safety_note: The subgroup pattern means the pooled finding should not be generalized to younger adults, shorter exposures, or all curcumin formulations.

evidence.study_type: GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants across randomized Nigella sativa supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 GRADE-assessed synthesis of 82 randomized trials involving 5,026 participants reported pooled improvements across several glycemic and blood-pressure biomarkers with Nigella sativa.
evidence.evidence_grade: large systematic review/meta-analysis; surrogate cardiometabolic outcomes
evidence.safety_note: Interventions varied widely in dose, form, and duration, and pooled biomarker changes do not establish treatment of diabetes or prevention of cardiovascular events.

evidence.study_type: GRADE-based systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants across randomized ginger supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 GRADE-based meta-analysis of 36 randomized trials found reductions in waist circumference and body-fat percentage and an increase in adiponectin with ginger, while body weight and BMI were not significantly improved.
evidence.safety_note: The null body-weight and BMI findings are an important counterweight to broad weight-loss claims; adiponectin is a biomarker and does not itself establish clinical benefit.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.sample_size: randomized trials included in a 2026 meta-analysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis found no significant overall effect of cranberry consumption on C-reactive protein or interleukin-6, with substantial between-study heterogeneity.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; overall null inflammatory-marker findings
evidence.safety_note: Selected subgroup analyses showed increases in CRP or IL-6 in some populations or powder-form interventions, so the evidence does not support a universal anti-inflammatory claim.

evidence.study_type: systematic review of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants in randomized metabolic-health trials of fenugreek-derived preparations
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 systematic review of 50 randomized trials found glycemic effects of fenugreek-derived preparations were more consistent than effects on body weight or BMI.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; heterogeneous preparations and metabolic outcomes
evidence.safety_note: Seed powder, seed extract, and leaf extract studies differed substantially in participants, dose, and duration; results should not be generalized across preparations.

evidence.effect_or_condition: global cognition, working memory, and processing speed
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of human studies
evidence.population: participants in human curcumin cognition studies
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 synthesis of 10 human studies found no significant overall effect on global cognition, while subgroup analyses reported improvements in working memory and processing speed.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; global null with domain-specific subgroup signals
evidence.safety_note: The review reported a higher incidence of adverse events in curcumin groups than controls; domain-specific subgroup findings should not be reframed as broad cognitive enhancement.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized magnesium supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 meta-analysis of 38 randomized trials involving 2,709 participants found modest pooled reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure with magnesium supplementation.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; modest blood-pressure effect with high heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Effects were stronger in hypertensive or hypomagnesemic subgroups, were not significant in normotensive groups, and no clear dose-response relationship was identified.

evidence.population: participants with metabolic-syndrome components in placebo-controlled berberine trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 placebo-controlled meta-analysis reported reductions in triglycerides, fasting glucose, waist circumference, LDL cholesterol, and total cholesterol with berberine, while HDL cholesterol and systolic and diastolic blood pressure were not significantly changed.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; mixed metabolic biomarker outcomes
evidence.safety_note: The pooled analysis found no significant safety difference versus placebo, but short-duration effects varied for some outcomes and the evidence does not establish replacement of standard metabolic treatment.

evidence.effect_or_condition: human sleep outcomes across systematic reviews
evidence.study_type: scoping review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
evidence.population: human sleep populations represented across systematic reviews
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 scoping review covering 57 systematic reviews and 227 meta-analyses found that most inactive-comparator syntheses favored melatonin, but definitions and measurement of sleep quality varied substantially.
evidence.evidence_grade: overview-level evidence; broad positive direction with substantial methodological heterogeneity
evidence.safety_note: Only a small minority of included reviews met all predefined methodological-rigor criteria, and adverse-event terminology was inconsistent; common reported events were generally mild.

evidence.study_type: systematic review of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: participants with major depressive disorder or bipolar depression receiving adjunctive creatine
evidence.sample_size: 5 randomized trials; creatine n=126 and placebo n=112
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 systematic review found the psychiatric randomized evidence for creatine was small, short-term, and entirely adjunctive; one major-depression trial showed a large augmentation signal while other included trials were null.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; small heterogeneous adjunctive psychiatric evidence base
evidence.safety_note: Two creatine-treated participants in relevant trials experienced hypomania or mania. The evidence does not establish creatine as standalone or long-term treatment for mood disorders.

evidence.effect_or_condition: cognition and daily function in dementia and mild cognitive impairment
evidence.study_type: Cochrane systematic review of randomized studies
evidence.population: people with cognitive complaints, mild cognitive impairment, or dementia
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 Cochrane review of 82 studies involving 10,613 participants found small low-certainty cognitive and activities-of-daily-living signals in dementia, while ginkgo probably had little or no effect in mild cognitive impairment.
evidence.evidence_grade: Cochrane systematic review; low-certainty dementia signals and MCI null findings
evidence.safety_note: Heterogeneity in dementia outcomes was very high. Overall adverse-event rates were similar to placebo in pooled dementia trials, but the evidence does not support healthy-adult nootropic claims.
